Every affine fiber automorphism has continuous determinant of modulus one. Pullback is invertible on affine hyperplane parameters, fixes the mark, preserves exact cap masses, and transports the coarea derivative by the tangential determinant divided by continuous-normal length.

The positive balance covers the entire own plane, so equal own-fiber cap masses cannot all vanish. If all were full, each affine margin would be nonnegative on the interior and their weighted sum would vanish, contradicting nonzero continuous normals. Each own cut is proper and contributes positive coarea.

A minimal subset with zero in the convex hull has positive balancing coefficients and at most d+1 rows. Fixed-mark and fixed-centroid equations make the common centroid margin affine in z and zero at p, so a maximizing exposed vertex makes it nonnegative for every selected row.

A finite affine exposure penalty isolates the selected fiber uniformly in the outward unit normal. Its radial flux integrates to d times the whole volume. In a parallel central cap the new planar boundary has zero radial flux, and its intersection with the old boundary has zero surface measure because the plane passes through an interior point. The endpoint version holds for d=1.

Full-mass Grünbaum at the exposed centroid gives the required rowwise ratio; nonnegative inclusion preserves it for the original offset caps. Each normalized coarea response weight is a valid probability mixture of these rows.
